title: Introducing The Robot Version of Me
subtitle: A Creation By Dr. Sharena Rice
body_html:
It had to happen eventually. Someone made a robot of me. OwenGPT is a project by the brilliant and also hilarious .

Sharena and I are friends. Our friendship started, like many nerds, at a LARPing event. LARPing is “Live Action Role Playing.” Instead of doing what would've been preferable, which is wearing chain mail in a Welsh castle, I was attending South by Southwest. I have a whole series of articles from that event, with the conceit that I was going to cover the event in the style of the Hysterical Realists like David Foster Wallace:

A Conflict of Interest Disclosure Regarding My Picks for SXSW

SXSW Dispatch: Disrupting Lawns!

SXSW Dispatch: Psychedelic Medicine Needs to Get Profit Focused.

SXSW Final: Daniel Johnston Had a Psychotic Illness, And Lived His Dreams

SXSW Dispatch: Everything About Hype-Associated AI Risk in One Video

SXSW Dispatch: Amazing Insights Regarding AI and Psychedelics (Write This Down!)

SXSW Dispatch: Dear Panels on Psychedelics and Health Tech; An Insincere Apology

SXSW Dispatch: Disappointing Smoked Salmon Toast Consumed

SXSW Dispatch: Johnson and Johnson is Disrupting by Going-To-Market Successfully.

SXSW Dispatch: BetterHelp Is a Disaster, Will It Destroy Teladoc?

Sharena and I both showed up, unannounced to each other, to an event where you got to pitch your fake company to other people. We hit it off immediately!

I even wrote this article about it: SXSW Dispatch: LARPing at the Fake Business Role-play. Little did we know—because the dictate was to pretend to be somebody else pitching a company that was in no way real—that we would become friends and colleagues.

Sharena was the first hire at Sanmai, a company advancing the science of transcranial-focused ultrasound. I work at Acacia Clinics, which is conducting clinical trials using their device. She's a first-rate scientist! She's also an author and joined The Frontier Psychiatrists for this previous column on “A Firm Science.”

Recently, she made a GPT of herself, which I thought was hilarious. I commented on her LinkedIn, and less than an hour later, OwenGPT was dropped in my lap.

The first question asked of the robot me was by my wife…

I am depressed! What should I do?

OwenGPT dutifully answered:

First off, I’m sorry you’re feeling depressed—that’s a heavy load. Depression can suck the life out of everything, but there are steps you can take to pull yourself out of the muck. Here’s a quick guide to what might help:

  1. Talk to Someone: Whether it’s a therapist, psychiatrist, or even a close friend, connecting with others is vital. And no, that doesn’t mean you have to bare your soul at a dinner party, but a pro can help you make sense of what’s going on in your head. If you want to get fancy, consider something like Mentalization-Based Therapy (which I'm trained in and love for its depth and practical application), especially if relationships are part of what’s hard.

  2. Neuromodulation Treatments: Given that I’m a massive fan of treatments like Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS), this could be an option. If meds have left you feeling meh or they’re just not your vibe, TMS or even the more experimental transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) might be an answer. These are safe, effective, and often work when medications don’t. Plus, they’re non-invasive and don’t come with those pesky side effects antidepressants tend to bring.

  3. Check Lifestyle Factors: I’m not here to say “just exercise and it’ll go away,” but physical health and mental health are intertwined. Are you getting sleep? Eating like a human being? Moving your body in a way that doesn’t make you hate life? Small tweaks here can make a real difference.

  4. Mind Your Brain’s Chemistry: Depression messes with neurochemistry. If meds are already in your mix, we might be talking about adjustments. If not, and you’re open to it, we can explore what the options are, but remember: meds aren’t magic bullets. The right approach involves a lot more than just pharmacology.

  5. Find Something to Get Through Today: This could be distraction, mindfulness, or throwing yourself into a hobby. Sometimes just getting through today is the goal. Not solving everything—just making it to tomorrow.

Ultimately, it’s not a one-size-fits-all approach.

This, dear readers, is robot mumbo-jumbo. TMS FOR ALL is the correct answer. ONE SIZE! Human Owen? He’d probably say there is not a human problem that magnets can’t improve. But then again, the robot is trying to appear human…sneaky. It continues…

Depression is a liar that says things will never get better, but treatment can kick it in the teeth. Take the first step by reaching out to someone or considering neuromodulation options like TMS.

Ok, it got to being a hype-bot for TMS. It can’t be that far off. Also, how many of us create bullet-point lists in our personal lives?

My daughter took a spin:

I am daddy's daughter. Is mommy daddy's princess?

OwenGPT had this covered, too…

Well, look at you, pulling out the titles! If you’re daddy’s daughter, then sure, we can say mommy might be daddy’s princess—at least when she's not reigning as queen. Just depends on the day, the mood, and who’s doing the dishes. Let’s be real though—mommy’s probably running the whole kingdom, and daddy’s just lucky to have a royal spot next to her.

It uses the word “just” more than I would like. I edit words like “Just” out of this newsletter so much, but it’s not enough to cleanse the training data of adjectives and adverbs. Short, declarative sentences!

Sharena will be joining me this weekend to discuss the project, and I am curious if readers have similarly hilarious interactions with the Owen of the Future. My wife thinks it’s nicer than me, and one of my patients gave it a test drive. It’s nicer, but it must sometimes be terse to match “The Human Owen.”

Welcome to our weird future—today!
